title: Visual Programming C# - Week 5 & Week 6 MCQ Bank
source: Week 5 and Week 6 lecture slides by Dr. Saad Adnan

questions.question: Who normally decides the order of operations in the lecture’s traditional Console example?
questions.explanation: Console follows the order of statements.

questions.question: In a GUI control-panel example, who chooses whether Add, Edit, or Delete happens first?
questions.explanation: The user chooses the next action.

questions.question: In the comparison slide, GUI input can be read:
options: At any time from multiple controls
questions.explanation: Controls can receive user input at different times.

questions.question: Which is the typical Console output described in the comparison?
questions.explanation: Console output is presented as text lines in the lecture.

questions.question: Which call reads a line of input in C# Console?
questions.explanation: ReadLine reads the user-entered line.

questions.question: What does int.Parse(Console.ReadLine()) try to produce?
questions.explanation: int.Parse converts the entered numeric text to int.

questions.question: Inversion of Control in the WPF example means:
options: The framework calls your registered handlers
questions.explanation: WPF decides when to call the handler.

questions.question: What does button.Click += OnClick do?
options: Register OnClick for the Click event
questions.explanation: += subscribes the method; it does not call it.

questions.question: Which of the following is a control PROPERTY?
questions.explanation: Width describes a control property.

questions.question: Which of the following is a control METHOD?
questions.explanation: Clear() is an action a control can perform.

questions.question: Which of the following is an EVENT?
questions.explanation: TextChanged indicates something happened.

questions.question: What does XAML / designer mainly define in this lecture?
questions.explanation: Appearance is assigned to XAML / designer.

questions.question: What does the dictionary key "add" represent in the mini event loop?
questions.explanation: The key identifies the command to handle.

questions.question: What construct repeats the Console event-loop demo?
questions.explanation: The while loop keeps accepting commands until break.

questions.question: In a real WPF GUI, who runs the event loop?
questions.explanation: WPF manages the event loop.

questions.question: What is an Event Handler?
options: The code responding to an event
questions.explanation: A handler executes when its subscribed event occurs.

questions.question: What is an Event Source?
options: The object where an event occurs
questions.explanation: The clicked Calculate button is the source.

questions.question: In the doorbell analogy, pressing the bell corresponds to:
questions.explanation: Pressing the bell is event occurrence.

questions.question: Which is a user-input event?
questions.explanation: KeyDown comes from user input.

questions.question: Which method is recommended for checking text before integer conversion?
questions.explanation: TryParse validates numeric text without throwing for bad format.

questions.question: Which pairing matches the slide’s program lifetime comparison?
options: Console until window closes; GUI until Main ends
Console when Main ends; GUI usually until closed
questions.explanation: These are the lecture’s typical lifetime cases.

questions.question: Which GUI response to invalid input is listed on the comparison slide?
options: Block, warn, or ignore per control
questions.explanation: GUI can block, warn, or ignore by control.

questions.question: A user typed a wrong name and already entered age. What is required in a simple Console flow to edit name?
questions.explanation: Going back requires extra Console logic.

questions.question: If name is "Ali" and age is 20, what does $"{name} is {age}" represent?
questions.explanation: String interpolation substitutes the variable values.

questions.question: Which description is accurate for Click += OnClick?
options: The handler is registered for a later click
questions.explanation: The subscription executes later on event raise.

questions.question: Which accurately describes the UI object tree?
options: Window contains panels that contain controls
questions.explanation: Window > panel > controls is the shown structure.

questions.question: In Dictionary<string, Action>, what is stored as the VALUE?
options: An Action referring to an operation
questions.explanation: The Action is the handler-like operation.

questions.question: What does the lambda () => Console.WriteLine("Add clicked") specify?
questions.explanation: The empty parentheses mean no parameters.

questions.question: What does TryGetValue(name, out Action? handler) do when key exists?
options: Returns true and supplies matching Action
questions.explanation: Lookup retrieves the action; calling happens separately.

questions.question: If the user enters "delete" without registration, the demo prints:
questions.explanation: Only add and clear are registered.

questions.question: Which statement ends the mini Console loop on "quit"?
questions.explanation: break exits the while loop.

questions.question: What does handler() in the Console demo correspond to in GUI?
questions.explanation: It illustrates dispatch to handler code.

questions.question: Which term means linking a handler to an event?
questions.explanation: Subscription registers a response.

questions.question: Which term describes WHICH key was pressed?
questions.explanation: Key details are event data.

questions.question: Which analogy element represents event source?
options: The one who opens the door
questions.explanation: The button is the origin of the ring.

questions.question: What happens immediately after Windows receives the click in the lecture’s journey?
questions.explanation: The message is placed in the application’s queue.

questions.question: Which is a window/lifecycle event?
questions.explanation: Closing belongs to window lifecycle.

questions.question: In the login example, Enter (KeyDown) on the window is intended to:
options: Behave as if Login was clicked
questions.explanation: Enter activates login behavior in the slide.

questions.question: Which event is used to focus the username box on form startup?
questions.explanation: Loaded triggers initialization in the login example.

questions.question: Why keep event handlers short according to the slides?
questions.explanation: A slow handler blocks UI response.

questions.question: Which is TRUE about registering an event handler?
options: Registration and invocation are different operations
Registration must happen after every click
questions.explanation: Registering says what should execute when the event occurs.

questions.question: Assume the user enters: add, clear, quit. How many times is a registered Action invoked?
questions.explanation: add and clear invoke Actions; quit breaks before lookup.

questions.question: Assume input is "ADD" while the registered key is "add". With default Dictionary<string, Action> comparison, what happens?
questions.explanation: Default string key comparison is case-sensitive.

questions.question: Which operation actually EXECUTES the retrieved Action?
questions.explanation: TryGetValue retrieves; handler() invokes.

questions.question: Which line would ADD a new recognized "delete" command using the same pattern?
questions.explanation: It assigns an Action under the delete key.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the name != null test before lookup?
options: To avoid using a null input as a dictionary key
questions.explanation: ReadLine may return null, so the check guards lookup.

questions.question: Which is the best match: WPF subscribing a handler vs Console demo?
questions.explanation: Storing an Action parallels registering a handler.

questions.question: If a button emits Click but no custom handler is subscribed, which lecture-level conclusion is correct?
questions.explanation: No registered handler means no application-specific response from it.

questions.question: What does the doorbell analogy emphasize about source and handler?
options: They must be the same object
The source knows every listener’s code
questions.explanation: Source does not need to know who handles its event.

questions.question: Put steps in correct lecture order: (1) WPF Dispatcher, (2) Windows receives, (3) App queue, (4) Handler runs.
questions.explanation: Windows receives -> queue -> Dispatcher -> handler, with Click raised before handler.

questions.question: The lecturer says your code appears in the second-to-last major step. Which step is that?
options: The click is generated by hardware
questions.explanation: Handler runs just before UI updated in the shown sequence.

questions.question: Which matched pair correctly distinguishes time and application-defined events?
questions.explanation: Tick is timer-related; OrderPlaced is user-defined.

questions.question: Which is the correct repeating lifecycle after initialization?
options: Event -> initialize UI again every time
questions.explanation: Handlers return control to the wait loop.

questions.question: Which login event-handler combination is correctly matched to the lecture?
options: Loaded -> Focus username and load settings
questions.explanation: The Loaded handler prepares the login form.

questions.question: A login form has unsaved content and the user tries to exit. Which event is most relevant?
questions.explanation: Closing is used to ask for confirmation.

questions.question: What is wrong with a handler that performs a long blocking calculation on the UI thread?
options: It forces all input to integers
It may freeze the window until complete
It cannot be a C# method
questions.explanation: UI-thread blocking delays event processing.

questions.question: Which technique follows BOTH “one handler, one job” and “do not copy-paste”?
options: Duplicate long code in all buttons
Put shared logic into helper methods
questions.explanation: Extract shared behavior and keep handlers focused.

questions.question: An app assumes Delete can only be clicked after Add. Which rule warns against this assumption?
options: Do not rely on order of unrelated events
questions.explanation: Users can invoke unrelated actions in different orders.

questions.question: What is the preferred response to numeric text "ABC" in a TextBox?
options: Validate using TryParse and show appropriate response
questions.explanation: TryParse guards invalid numeric input.

questions.question: Which statement captures the lecture’s design question for event-driven programs?
options: Which instruction must ALWAYS execute first?
How many times does Main loop?
What can the user do, and what should happen?
How do I eliminate all events?
questions.explanation: Design responses around user actions.

questions.question: In Demo 1, which control has Content="Click me"?
questions.explanation: The XAML creates a Button.

questions.question: Which XAML attribute connects the Button to Hello_Click?
questions.explanation: Click="Hello_Click" subscribes the handler in XAML.

questions.question: Which named control displays the click count?
questions.explanation: The TextBlock named lblOut receives the text.

questions.question: What is the initial value of clicks in Demo 1?
questions.explanation: The declaration is int clicks = 0.

questions.question: What does clicks++ do?
questions.explanation: It increments the variable.

questions.question: After ONE click in Demo 1, what is displayed?
questions.explanation: The counter goes 0 -> 1.

questions.question: After TWO clicks in Demo 1, what is displayed?
questions.explanation: The counter reaches 2.

questions.question: After THREE clicks in Demo 1, what is displayed?
questions.explanation: The counter reaches 3.

questions.question: What is the C# equivalent of Click="BtnSave_Click"?
questions.explanation: The C# += syntax registers the same method.

questions.question: What does the sample save handler show?
questions.explanation: MessageBox.Show displays Saved!.

questions.question: What is a delegate?
options: A reference to a method with a compatible signature
questions.explanation: A delegate is a type-safe method reference.

questions.question: Which built-in delegate type returns nothing (void)?
questions.explanation: Action delegates return void.

questions.question: Which built-in delegate type returns a value?
questions.explanation: Func has a return-value type parameter.

questions.question: What ready-made delegate is specifically associated with events?
questions.explanation: EventHandler is provided for event signatures.

questions.question: Which control allows choosing English or Spanish?
questions.explanation: cmbLang is the ComboBox.

questions.question: What is the initial delegate target in Demo 2a?
questions.explanation: greeter is initialized to English.

questions.question: Which greeting appears for Ali when English is selected and Greet is pressed?
questions.explanation: English formats Hello, Ali!.

questions.question: Which greeting appears for Ali after choosing Spanish and pressing Greet?
questions.explanation: Spanish formats Hola, Ali!.

questions.question: Which operator ADDS a subscriber to an event?
questions.explanation: += subscribes a handler.

questions.question: What does sender refer to in the standard handler signature?
options: The object that raised the event
questions.explanation: sender identifies the event source.

questions.question: In <TextBlock x:Name="lblOut" />, what is x:Name used for?
options: Naming the control so code can refer to it
questions.explanation: Code uses lblOut.Text to update the named TextBlock.

questions.question: What is the purpose of Margin="15" on StackPanel?
options: Set spacing around its content area
questions.explanation: Margin controls external spacing for the panel.

questions.question: Immediately after opening Demo 1, before any clicks, what runs?
options: No click handler has run yet
questions.explanation: The lecture explicitly says nothing runs yet.

questions.question: Which line updates the on-screen result after each click?
questions.explanation: The TextBlock Text property is set inside handler.

questions.question: Why should you NOT register the same handler in both XAML and C#?
options: It prevents compilation in every case
The handler can execute twice per click
questions.explanation: Duplicate subscription causes duplicate invocations.

questions.question: What does Action<string> show = SayHello; store?
questions.explanation: Assigning method name stores method reference.

questions.question: What does show("Ali") do?
options: Sets show equal to a string
questions.explanation: The delegate is invoked with the argument.

questions.question: What does "type-safe" mean for delegates in this context?
options: Any method can be assigned regardless of signature
Only compatible method signatures can be assigned
Methods must be declared in XAML
questions.explanation: The delegate’s required parameter and return types must match.

questions.question: What happens if a multicast delegate stores several methods and is invoked?
options: All stored methods are invoked in order
questions.explanation: The lecture specifies calling all methods in order.

questions.question: What is the type of greeter in Demo 2?
questions.explanation: The delegate accepts a string and returns a string.

questions.question: What does cmbLang.SelectedIndex == 1 select?
questions.explanation: Index 1 is Spanish in the shown list.

questions.question: In greeter = condition ? Spanish : English, what is ? : called?
questions.explanation: The conditional operator chooses one of two methods.

questions.question: What does Greet_Click actually call to obtain the greeting?
questions.explanation: The handler invokes the currently selected delegate.

questions.question: After typing Ali but BEFORE pressing Greet in the initial English state, the output is:
questions.explanation: Text appears only when greeting action is invoked.

questions.question: After changing the language from English to Spanish WITHOUT pressing Greet again, what happens to the existing label?
options: It immediately changes to Hola, Ali!
It stays Hello, Ali! until Greet is pressed
questions.explanation: Only the delegate target changes at selection time.

questions.question: In the publisher/subscriber model, who DECIDES when to raise an event?
questions.explanation: Event source owns the decision to raise its event.

questions.question: Which operator unsubscribes a handler?
questions.explanation: -= removes subscription.

questions.question: According to the event keyword safety rule, outside code can typically:
options: Assign the event to null freely
questions.explanation: External code is limited to add/remove handlers.

questions.question: Which standard handler signature is shown on the lecture slide?
questions.explanation: This is the standard EventHandler signature.

questions.question: Why does the standard event handler return void?
options: The source does not expect a return value
No code can run inside it
questions.explanation: The event source does not expect an answer.

questions.question: Starting with clicks = 0, what will lblOut.Text be after five clicks?
questions.explanation: Five handler executions increment from 0 to 5.

questions.question: Suppose Hello_Click is accidentally subscribed twice and clicks starts at 0. What is clicks after ONE physical click?
options: The project must fail to compile
questions.explanation: Both subscriptions invoke the handler, incrementing twice.

questions.question: Which pair produces the duplicate-registration warning in the lecture?
questions.explanation: Both register the same method for the same event.

questions.question: Which declaration is compatible with static void SayHello(string name)?
questions.explanation: SayHello takes string and returns void.

questions.question: If a method returns string from a string argument, which delegate shape best fits?
questions.explanation: Func<string,string> means string input and string output.

questions.question: Which statement is INCORRECT about delegates in these slides?
options: A delegate can be stored in a variable
A delegate can be called later
A delegate can reference multiple compatible methods
questions.explanation: Func can return values; delegates are not all void.

questions.question: An Action<string> delegate is assigned a method that requires TWO int parameters. What is the issue?
options: The event loop will fix it
questions.explanation: Parameter number/types must be compatible.

questions.question: In the Demo 2 ComboBox, index 0 maps to which method?
questions.explanation: The conditional selects English unless SelectedIndex is 1.

questions.question: If the selection becomes index 1, what is stored in greeter?
questions.explanation: The selected method reference replaces English.

questions.question: Which expression invokes the current greeting method using text from txtName?
questions.explanation: The delegate is called with the input text.

questions.question: Sequence: enter Ali, press Greet, switch to Spanish, do NOT press Greet. What is lblOut.Text?
questions.explanation: Switching changes the method pointer, not the existing display.

questions.question: Sequence: enter Ali, press Greet (English), switch to Spanish, press Greet. What is final output?
questions.explanation: The second click invokes Spanish and replaces TextBlock text.

questions.question: What remains unchanged when ComboBox language changes in Demo 2?
options: The button and Greet_Click handler code
questions.explanation: The handler is stable while delegate target changes.

questions.question: Which statement is the key distinction between an event and a plain delegate in the lecture?
options: Events can be invoked by any external code
Events add ownership/safety rules on raising
Plain delegates cannot refer to methods
questions.explanation: Only the event-owning class may raise its event.

questions.question: Which action is permitted to an external subscriber for an event?
options: Assign a new event invocation list
questions.explanation: Outside code can subscribe and unsubscribe.

questions.question: In publisher/subscriber terminology, the button in Demo 1 is the:
questions.explanation: The Button raises Click; Hello_Click is subscriber handler.

questions.question: In void Handler(object sender, EventArgs e), EventArgs e provides:
options: Event information; specialized types may add data
questions.explanation: EventArgs is base data, specialized event args add details.

questions.question: For a WPF Click handler, which second argument type does the demonstrated code use?
questions.explanation: Demo 1 uses RoutedEventArgs for Click.

questions.question: For a ComboBox SelectionChanged handler, which argument type is used in Demo 2?
questions.explanation: The Demo 2 selection handler uses SelectionChangedEventArgs.

questions.question: Which statement best captures the Publisher/Subscriber separation?
options: The publisher must know all handlers’ implementations
The publisher raises the event without needing to know who listens
Subscribers decide when publisher code executes
Every subscriber must return a string
questions.explanation: The publisher need not know its listeners.
